title: Research: save 3,276 JP8 scalar primitives per orientation with signed digits
head: d3bc41b87fc7d23f50d064a0f06f1a89e3ab02a7
body:
The selected JP8 supplier prepares every dyadic numerator with binary Horner. This finite local circuit improvement uses signed digits only when they reduce the complete primitive count, saving **3,276 real-component primitives per orientation**. **Status: research construction / finite circuit improvement; no new kappa.**

| JP8 orientation | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Forward | 257,232 | 253,956 | 3,276 |
| Backward | 257,280 | 254,004 | 3,276 |

The 250 changed additions per orientation preserve the complete target/source/private-scratch boundary map. Every source read, doubling, signed accumulation, halving and scratch clear is charged. The original initial clear/add and unit circuits remain, so these savings exclude concurrent #696's copy and unit-coefficient work.

Signed digits can overshoot the numerator by one. The exact forward envelope increases by `34078712/34078711`; the checker recomputes it rather than reusing the old receipt. Forward and backward bounds remain 64 and 101 bits, within the inherited 192-bit local allowance. Scalar macro words, frames, helpers, paid child profiles, adapters and restoration boundaries are unchanged.

Only `research/complex-signed-digit/` is added. It contains the executable primitive recipe, written argument, independent rational interpreter, deterministic receipt, five source pins, local claim and validation record.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-signed-digit/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_COMPLEX_SIGNED_DIGIT jp8 additions=250+250 real_saved=3276+3276 columns=716 controls=9`.

The offline standard-library check processes every event of both pinned JP8 programs, verifies all coefficient boundary maps, reconstructs the full 716-column scalar projection, recounts exact costs and prefix envelopes, and compares the committed receipt. Nine controls cover wrong signs, missing initialization/restoration/halving/accumulation, inadmissible coefficients, an undercharged scratch bound and an endpoint-neutral target excursion. Python 3.14.8 normal and isolated optimized runs pass; source/receipt corruption checks, `make selected-record-check` and staged whitespace checks pass.

Exact base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Selected #626 source: `660de893d27bb7abd1d5b01b1640207528a5c851`, with #622 at `f69477f4f6d3c7eb1f740b166881bffed4ffa9f6`. All consumed source bytes have SHA-256 and Git-blob pins; gzip inputs also have payload pins.

OS seed **36**, complex-supplier track. Three candidate tasks and the local claim are recorded. No pinned coordination issue exists. The overlap refresh covered 540 open PRs through #721 and refreshed #696, #681, #687 and #717. Numerator recoding adds a distinct incremental saving beyond #696; none of those pending PRs is an implementation dependency.

Concurrent **#722**, by @ellipsi2 at `a0766ab0fab379e1997fadc3ca157578d57986c1`, arrived between the final snapshot and submission and is now credited. It shares binary-Horner preparation across forward cleanup blocks. This contribution recodes individual numerators, preserves clearing after every macro, and also saves work backward, where #722 reports no eligible sharing runs. Its body and file inventory were inspected, but its implementation is neither imported nor independently verified here. No combined saving is claimed without a composed recount.

Credit to Jeremy Kothe and the #622 Claude Code contributors, Chafik Boukhalfa, icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds, Dugongue, eumemic and the retained predecessor notices. Prepared for **Sagar Thakrar (@thakrarsagar)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including a separately delegated mathematical/code cross-check. Apache-2.0; no independent human-review claim.

Full `make verify`, selected cold replay, global hosting/assembly, Linux CI and Lean were not run. All inherited compiler, physical hosting, precision/tape and analytic assumptions remain. This finite scalar check does not formalize the multiplication theorem or change the selected frontier. Integration must refresh the exact forward prefix receipt.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
